id.description: The id the profile keeps its values under: a word of lower-case letters, digits and `_`, 1 to 32.

help.description: A line saying what it sets.

harnesses.description: The ids of the harnesses it applies to, as the standard registry of harnesses names them (`claude-code`, the value of `AGENTS_HARNESS`); none means every harness.

schema.description: The values it takes, as a guatiao schema of an object whose members are what its form asks for; none for an item that takes no values. A member the schema marks sensitive is never shown in clear.

form.description: How the schema is shown, a guatiao-intake form document (sections, widgets, `visibleWhen`); none shows the form the schema implies.

harness.description: The id of the harness the session runs, as [`ItemInfo::harnesses`] names it; empty when it has none, so an item may differ by harness.

values.description: What the profile holds for the item, as an object keyed by the schema's member names; a member left empty is absent.

env.description: Variables the session's programs are given. A variable the profile's own environment already sets keeps that value, and the report says so.

args.description: Arguments added to the command line of a program the host starts.

value.description: Its value, as text (`true` or `false` for a yes or no).

settings.description: Values of the session's own settings.

route.description: The name of a route the host has: `system`, `direct` or one of `[network.routes]`. A route the host lacks, or one that does not open, refuses the session's start.

hosts.description: The destinations it is for, each a host name, `*.name`, an address or a regular expression ([`HostPattern`]); none means every destination no other rule names.

routes.description: The routes, in order. Empty leaves the session on the host's route.

bypass.description: Hosts that go direct, in the `NO_PROXY` form; empty keeps what the routes choose.

pattern.title: Hosts
pattern.description: A host name (`api.example.com`), a name and everything under it (`*.example.com`), an address, or any other regular expression, matched whole and without regard to case against the destination as the program names it (a name, or an address): `.*` matches every destination, `(api|auth)[.]example[.]com` two.

identity.title: Certificate
identity.description: `system` presents what the operating system's keystores choose by the authorities the server names, as a browser would; or the thumbprint (SHA-256, in hex) of one certificate the host lists as available.

intercept.description: The destinations whose TLS the host's proxy for the session ends, so as to present a client certificate to them, in order: the first entry whose pattern matches a destination says which certificate it gets; every destination no entry matches stays a tunnel the program's own TLS runs through.

network.description: The routes its programs' network leaves by.

notes.description: What the report says of it, a line each, in the person's words.
